🍫 Si t’agrada la xocolata i visites Luxemburg, apunta’t aquest lloc.

La Chocolate House by Nathalie Bonn, just davant del Palau Gran Ducal, és una d’aquelles parades que intento repetir cada vegada que torno a la ciutat. 🇱🇺

I una de les seves especialitats més curioses són les Chocospoons: blocs de xocolata amb una cullera que desfàs remenant-los en llet calenta. I el més difícil és escollir entre tots els gustos que tenen. 🤤

Me la van recomanar fa anys… i ara ja s’ha convertit en una parada obligatòria per a mi. ❤️

items.summary:

5 funded programmes that can get you to Luxembourg for free 🇱🇺🔥

These are paid traineeships at official EU institutions based in Luxembourg. They cover your monthly salary and some include travel support. Open to graduates from various fields.

Here are all 5 👇🏾

1️⃣ CJEU Traineeship (Court of Justice of the EU)
💰 €2,400/month (highest paid EU traineeship)
📅 5 months (March to July 2027)
📋 Not just for law graduates. IT, engineering, economics, political science, architecture all welcome
⏰ Deadline: 15 September 2026
🔗 curia.europa.eu

2️⃣ European Court of Auditors (ECA) Traineeship
💰 Paid traineeship
📅 6 months
📋 University graduates across various fields. Auditing, admin, communications, translation, IT, legal
📍 Luxembourg City
🔗 eca.europa.eu

3️⃣ Blue Book Traineeship (European Commission)
💰 €1,538/month for Luxembourg placements
📅 5 months
📋 Limited slots for non EU nationals but they do exist
⏰ Current cycle closed. Reopens twice a year. Watch for next window.
🔗 traineeships.ec.europa.eu

4️⃣ Schuman Traineeship (European Parliament)
💰 €1,667/month + €300 travel grant
📅 5 months
📋 502 places per session. Luxembourg placements available.
⏰ Applications: 1 to 31 October 2026
🔗 europarl.europa.eu/traineeships

5️⃣ EIB Traineeship (European Investment Bank)
💰 €1,500 to €1,900/month + travel support + insurance
📅 1 to 5 months
📋 Mainly EU nationals but dedicated MENA/ACP track for non EU applicants
⏰ Individual deadlines per vacancy
🔗 eib.org/en/about/careers

The CJEU deadline is 15 September 2026. That is 9 days away. If you are a graduate, apply NOW.

“I hate living in Luxembourg, is so boring😭”

Meanwhile, there are a lot of events that you are missing ‘cause you’re not looking in the right places!

As a Sicilian, I have a different definition of “boring” 😂 If you think Luxembourg is boring, you’ve clearly never lived on an island where the biggest event of the weekend is a village festival in the middle of nowhere, 40 minutes from civilization and absolutely no chance of getting there without a car.

Meanwhile, Luxembourg has concerts, festivals, exhibitions, markets, parties and events happening all year round.

So no, Luxembourg is NOT boring. You just have to know where to look 👀🇱🇺

items.summary:
Luxembourg's Largest Funfair - Save & plan your annual-visit to this iconic event in Luxembourg city... ✨🎡🎠

With history dating back to the early 14th century, this festival has evolved into one of the most iconic events in Luxembourg & the Greater Region. It originally started as a trade & livestock market (stop between Flanders & Italy).

Nowadays, you can experience a gigantic funfair with food, games and live music across 4 hectares - directly in the heart of Luxembourg's city centre.

This year welcomes brand NEW additions - including the Virtual Reality Experience "Dr Archibald : Master of Time" and high-speed thrill ride "Skater".

On the last day of the event each year (this year on 09.09.2026), you can enjoy all attractions at half price. What's more - a FREE firework display will illuminate the skies at 22:00 on the Grand Duchess Charlotte Bridge - so make sure to take note & plan your visit (before it's too late!)

📍Schueberfouer, Luxembourg City 🇱🇺

Arrival: Use the free public transport - Luxtram "T1" to the stop "Theater". 

Entry: Free entry to the grounds

Opening times: Every day between 12:00 and 01:00 until 09.09.2026

FOLLOW me for all the best travel tips, tricks and advice & turn on the notifications bell! 🔔🌎
-
Das größte Volksfest Luxemburgs und der Großregion - Speichere dir dieses Video und plane deinen Besuch auf die Schueberfouer. ✨🎡🎠🩵🗺️

Die Geschichte der Schueberfouer geht bis ins 14. Jahrhundert zurück, als das Fest ursprünglich als Handelsmarkt gegründet wurde.

Heutzutage kann man eine gigantische Kirmes mit diversen Fahrgeschäften & Live Musik miterleben - direkt mitten in der Stadt Luxemburg.

Das diesjährige Event begrüßt viele neuen Highlights und der Abschluss wird am 09.09.2026 mit einem kostenlosen Feuerwerk gekrönt.

Also... plane deinen Besuch auf die Schueberfouer , bevor es zu spät ist…!

3. 🌍 Un pays très international:on y rencontre des personnes de nombreuses nationalités et plusieurs langues sont parlées.           4. 🎓 De bonnes possibilités d’études:écoles et formations avec un environnement très international.                                            5. ✈️ Une position idéale en Europe:la France, l’Allemagne et la Belgique sont juste à côté, pratique pour voyager.

HOW TO MOVE TO LUXEMBOURG? 🇱🇺 READ THIS 👇

Luxembourg has affordable study options AND paid traineeship opportunities.

🎓 University of Luxembourg
Many programmes cost around €400/semester.
🔗 uni.lu/study

1. CJEU Traineeship
🎓 Opportunities across IT, HR, communications, finance, engineering, translation & more
💰 ~€2,400/month + travel allowance
⏳ 5 months
🔗 curia.europa.eu

2. European Court of Auditors (ECA)
🎓 Opportunities for university graduates across various fields
💰 Paid traineeship
⏳ Usually 3–6 months
📍 Luxembourg City
🔗 eca.europa.eu

3. BLUE BOOK TRAINEESHIP
🇪🇺 European Commission
• 5 months
• Around €1,572/month for Luxembourg placements
• Limited opportunities for non-EU nationals
📅 Deadline: 4 Sept 2026 ( it will reopen again- it’s twice a year) 
🔗 traineeships.ec.europa.eu

4. SCHUMAN TRAINEESHIP
🇪🇺 European Parliament
• 5 months
• Paid monthly grant
• Luxembourg placements available
📅 Applications: 1–30 Nov 2026
🔗 europarl.europa.eu/traineeships

5. EIB TRAINEESHIP
🏦 European Investment Bank, Luxembourg
• Around €1,500/month
• Usually 3–5 months
• Travel support available
⚠️ Standard programme mainly for EU/EU-candidate nationals but they have slots for non-EU applicants 
📅 Vacancies have individual deadlines
🔗 eib.org/en/about/careers/categories/traineeships

⚠️ Eligibility varies. These are competitive opportunities and do not guarantee visas, jobs or permanent residence.

items.summary:
Le Luxembourg est le pays dans lequel les Français sont le moins bien accueillis. 🇱🇺
C’est parce qu’ils ne respectent pas assez la culture luxembourgeoise.
Les Français n’osent pas employer la langue luxembourgeoise pour dire bonjour quand ils rentrent dans un commerce.
C’est simple et ça montre le respect qu’on a pour les gens.
Les Français à l’étranger ont mauvaise réputation, que ça soit à New York ou en Thaïlande.
Vous ne pouvez pas vous attendre à être traités comme à la maison, il faut faire des efforts d’intégration.
Faites preuve d’ouverture et de respect lorsque vous n’êtes pas en France. 🇫🇷

items.summary:
Publi l GUARDA este destino, ¡te encantará! ✈️🇱🇺
Es un país pequeño, pero tiene una mezcla brutal de castillos, pueblos medievales, naturaleza, viñedos y una capital con muchísimo que ver. 

📍 Lugares que visitamos:
▪️Valle de los 7 Castillos: una ruta de unos 25 km que conecta castillos y mansiones históricas y recorre más de 1.000 años de historia.
▪️ Luxemburgo Ciudad: no te pierdas el Chemin de la Corniche, el barrio de Grund, las Casamatas del Bock, el Palacio Gran Ducal y el ascensor panorámico de Pfaffenthal.
▪️ Vianden: uno de nuestros favoritos. Pasea por su pueblo medieval, sube en el único telesilla del país para verlo desde las alturas y visita su impresionante castillo.
▪️ Mullerthal: si te gusta la naturaleza, apunta la ruta B2 de Berdorf. Son solo 4,35 km (1 h 20 min aprox.) y pasa entre cañones, formaciones rocosas, cuevas y miradores.
▪️ Mosela: conduce entre viñedos y sube hasta el mirador de Wormer Koeppchen.
▪️ Schengen: aquí se firmó en 1985 el histórico Acuerdo de Schengen. Puedes visitar el monumento y el museo dedicado a su historia.

💡El transporte público en Luxemburgo es gratuito, así que puedes moverte en tren, tranvía y autobús sin pagar billete.

Nosotros hicimos esta ruta en 4 días y es un destino perfecto si quieres combinar ciudad, castillos y naturaleza sin hacer distancias enormes.
